correctionNotes: Sub-bass is well-extended and robust; no major correction is needed below 100 Hz.

The dip around 2 kHz is a signature acoustic characteristic of Denon/Fostex wood cups. Over-correcting this region (e.g. by applying a large +6dB boost) will destroy the natural soundstage depth and introduce boxy cup reflections. Keep this upper-mid dip mostly intact, or apply only a very gentle correction (e.g., < +2dB).
Cut the sibilance/harshness peak around 5.4-5.5 kHz with a narrow bell filter (~ -4 to -6 dB, Q ~ 3.0) to remove metallic glare.
Smooth the piercing peak in the upper treble (11-13 kHz) with a high-shelf or bell filter to prevent fatiguing sibilance without sacrificing wood's airy resolution.
Avoid EQing the 8.5 kHz dip as it is likely a coupler measurement notch.
signature: Warm, spacious closed-back wood sound: robust sub-bass, relaxed upper-mids (2kHz dip), and bright treble with peaks at 5.5kHz and 11-13kHz.
source: Crinacle frequency response graph measurement (GRAS 43AG-7) - 2026-06-16. Closed-back Japanese bamboo wood cups.
